author: Vitor
notes: A brute-force solution, not a very smart one.
aiExplanation: This is a **brute-force** solution that tries every triplet of indices `(i, j, k)` with `i <= j <= k`, computes the **XOR** of the three corresponding values, and adds each result to a `Set` to automatically discard duplicates, finally returning the set's size as the count of unique XOR values. It runs in `O(n^3)` time, which is too slow and causes a **time limit exceeded**.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution skips computing any XOR values directly and instead relies on a **mathematical shortcut**: since any triplet from `nums` can XOR together to produce every value up to the next power of two above `n` (once there are enough elements to combine), the answer is simply `n` itself when there are 2 or fewer numbers, or otherwise the **smallest power of two greater than or equal to `n`**, found by left-shifting `ans` until it exceeds `n`.
